api: REST API for the hosted service; locally, whatever pipeline you build.
cons: Licence terms vary by release and need reading each time
name: Stable Diffusion
pros: Fully self-hostable, nothing leaves your infrastructure
files: Text prompts, image inputs, masks, and control inputs depending on the pipeline.
value: Open-weight image generation that can run entirely on your own hardware. The only mainstream option where confidential visual work never leaves the building, and the base for most of the fine-tuning ecosystem.
engine: Stability AI's open-weight diffusion models, in several generations and sizes.
latency: Hardware dependent. Fast on a capable GPU, slow on CPU.
quality: Very good, and highly controllable through the surrounding tooling. Base output aesthetics generally trail Midjourney; controllability is far ahead.
tagline: The open-weight image model that made local, private image generation possible.
use_cases: Generating imagery on confidential product or brand material locally
Fine-tuning a model on an organization's own visual style
integrations: The broad open ecosystem of interfaces and fine-tuning tools
governance_note: Licensing is the thing to check, not capability. Stability's model licences have changed across releases and some carry revenue-linked commercial conditions, so the licence attached to the specific checkpoint matters more than the family name. Separately, the training-data provenance litigation affecting the category applies here too: self-hosting removes the data-exposure risk but not the copyright question about outputs.
training_optout: Self-hosted use means nothing leaves your infrastructure. Hosted use follows Stability's terms.
